newsitem.title: USA: Florida jury to hear closing arguments in GM case.
newsitem.headline: Florida jury to hear closing arguments in GM case.

text.p: Jurors will return to court on Tuesday to hear closing arguments in the punitive damage phase of a product liability case against General Motors Corp., a judge ordered on Friday.

The jurors have been asked to fine the automotive giant between $50 million and $75 million by the family of a woman who suffered severe brain damage in a 1991 collision involving a Chevrolet Astro mini-van. The same jury in December ordered GM to pay $25 million to the former Jacksonville woman.
In the punitive damage phase of the case, which began Wednesday, jurors heard from a Yale economist who testified that a $75 million penalty would have a "negligible" financial impact on the company.
But General Motors presented witnesses who testified that the company's U.S. operations were not profitable between 1985 and 1995, and suffered a cumulative loss of $8.7 billion.
On Friday, an expert witness hired by the automaker testified about GM's accounting methods and details contained in the company's annual report to shareholders.
Circuit Judge Lawrence Fay asked the six-member jury to return to court at 9 a.m. EST on Tuesday for closing arguments in the case.
